name: Dr Justin Olstein
title: Contact Psychologist
description: My therapeutic philosophy centres around understanding how relational dynamics contribute to common client concerns. My therapy is compassionate, individualised, and guided by an interest in exploring how our past experiences shape our present-day concerns, paying close attention to the varied and subtle ways this can occur. I primarily draw upon psychodynamic and schema therapy approaches to help clients build a detailed and nuanced understanding of their relational selves. I have a wealth of experience working in public mental health settings, as well as in private practice, and has particular experience working with LGBTQIA+ clients. I work with: trauma, attachment issues, emotion regulation, self-esteem, life transitions, substance-related issues, family and relationship concerns, mood and anxiety concerns, sexuality exploration/identification, body image, cultural identity, grief/loss, fertility/IVF/surrogacy, and adjustment issues.
specialties: Adult survivors of sexual abuse, Sexual abuse, Diverse genders, Gender Dysphoria, Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Sexual difficulties, Diverse sexualities, Schema Therapy

name: Dr Daniel Shaw
title: Medicare Psychologist Provider
description: Dr. Daniel Shaw is a counselling and clinical psychologist who works with adults, couples, and adolescents. With a compassionate and collaborative approach, he helps clients navigate challenges related to trauma (PTSD, cPTSD, sexual assault, domestic violence, childhood abuse), OCD, eating disorders, anxiety, relationship issues, and behavioural addictions, such as gaming and pornography. He integrates evidence-based approaches, including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and Eye-Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR) to create tailored treatment plans that support lasting change and personal growth.
specialties: Adult survivors of sexual abuse, Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Sexual abuse, Diverse sexualities, Partners/families of sex offenders, Sexual difficulties, EMDR
